about: The crisis and continuity plan for the SecuRAX estate itself (doc 84): each scenario names how you notice it, the most downtime it may cause (RTO) and the most data it may lose (RPO), the steps in order, and a safe drill. `./securax continuity` measures the real RPO from your backups and mirrors, and the real RTO from your last drill. Edit this file, not the code.

scenarios.title: A change or update broke the estate
scenarios.notice: The Command Center or Chat stops answering after an update; ./securax ready says NOT READY.
steps: Go back to the last working version: ./securax rollback
Check it answers: ./securax ready
Diagnose calmly afterwards: ./securax why

scenarios.title: GitHub is down, or the account or repository is lost
scenarios.notice: ./securax update says it cannot reach the code; CI does not run; the website does not update.
steps: Nothing stops: the estate runs from your laptop and needs GitHub only for updates.
Check the local copy of the code is whole: ./securax continuity drill github-down
Keep working: commits stay local; ./securax verify runs every check on the laptop.
Point at the mirror: git remote set-url origin, followed by the GitLab address that MIRROR_REMOTES in local/compose/.env lists (none yet? ./securax continuity mirror setup)
On a new machine without GitHub: git clone <backup folder>/repo-latest.bundle ai-cloud-cyber-range

scenarios.title: The laptop is lost, stolen or dead
scenarios.notice: You no longer have the machine.
steps: Revoke what the laptop held: change the AI provider keys and the Tailscale device (./securax keys lists them).
On the new machine: install WSL and Docker, then clone the code (GitHub, the mirror, or repo-latest.bundle from the off-site folder).
Bring the data back: ./securax restore <newest file in the off-site folder> (it needs your backup key: the second copy you saved).
Start and check: ./securax go

scenarios.title: Data corrupted, deleted or encrypted by ransomware
scenarios.notice: Chats, workflows or registers are missing or unreadable.
steps: Stop the estate so nothing overwrites more: ./securax down
If it looks like ransomware, keep the laptop off the network and follow ./securax respond.
Restore the newest good backup: ./securax restore <file> (off-site copy if the local ones are hit)
Change every key in .env afterwards: they may have been read.

scenarios.title: The backup key is lost
scenarios.notice: ./securax backup drill cannot open the off-site copy.
steps: Use the second copy you saved with ./securax protect (USB stick or password manager).
If no copy exists: make a new key now (./securax protect) and take a fresh backup at once; the old encrypted backups cannot be opened.

scenarios.title: An AI provider is down, or a key is revoked or over its limit
scenarios.notice: Answers slow down or come from the local model.
steps: Nothing to do at once: every chain falls to the next provider and ends on the local model.
See which models answer: ./securax models
Replace the key: ./securax providers add <id>

scenarios.title: The disk is full
scenarios.notice: Containers stop or refuse to start; your phone gets the storage alert.
steps: Run the safe clean-ups: ./securax storage --auto
See what is large: ./securax storage
Move Docker's disk to a bigger drive (doc 80).

scenarios.title: The estate itself may be compromised (a leaked key, an odd login, an unknown process)
scenarios.notice: An alert, an unknown device on Tailscale, or audit lines you do not recognise.
steps: Stop all AI at once: ./securax ai stop all --reason "suspected compromise"
Start the incident clock and keep evidence: ./securax incident open and ./securax respond
Change every key in .env and rotate the gateway keys.
When clean: ./securax ai resume all

scenarios.title: You are locked out of a key account (Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Tailscale, a cloud)
scenarios.notice: A sign-in fails and recovery is needed.
steps: Use the recovery codes kept in your password manager (./securax start passwords).
Follow the provider's account recovery; meanwhile the estate keeps running offline.
